articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Wars is in a very strange place in 2026. The franchise has been under Disney ownership for over a decade and the best way to describe the reception is mixed. The sequel trilogy has its fans, but it also has its naysayers. Rogue One was a hit with fans, but Solo wasn't. The shows have run of the gamut of being beloved like The Mandalorian , being hated like The Acolyte , and no one ever talking about them, like Skeleton Crew . However, there is a Star Wars show that is both loved by fans and critics alike – Andor . This show is one of the best pieces of Star Wars media ever , if not the greatest, and four years ago it proved it by giving us one of the coolest action scenes ever, one that rivaled the movies.

The first season of Andor was something of a revelation for fans. The varying quality of Star Wars media (I was going to type "in the Disney era", but let's be real – the quality of Star Wars has always been all over the place) meant that no one really knew what kind of show we were going to get before it started. The show impressed right away and it did it by being both the most Star Wars thing ever and also completely different from another Star War (take some money to go see one). However, the penultimate episode included an action scene that was pure Star Wars , rivaling anything fans had seen on the big screen.

Before Andor , Star Wars media was basically just adventure stories. Sure, there were deeper themes to the whole thing, but for the most part, it was just a modernization of the adventure serials that George Lucas watched a child. While the franchise played with fascism, rebellion, spirituality, family dynamics, and the like, it was first and foremost an exciting war in the stars (well, when it all worked out). Andor was originally very different from what we got , but the show was never going to be typical Star Wars .

I'm going to take a second out to define "typical Star Wars ", so we all know where I'm starting from. Star Wars typically is grandiose battles between good and evil, defined by the lightsaber fights that are metaphors for the clashing of opposing ideologies and massive space battle scenes. When it all works right, these types of action scenes are cathartic moments in the narrative, their pulse-pounding action bringing the stories to their culmination.

Andor was very short on typical Star Wars . While the show opened with Andor killing someone while looking for his sister, it wasn't the kind of exciting Star Wars scene we were used to; it was something out of a spy thrilller or a crime movie. I've experienced a lot of types of Star Wars stories over the decades – I was an avid EU readers up until the Disney purchase – and Andor was very much unique in the annals of the franchise, especially for fans who never ventured past the movies (if you want something amazing that isn't even close to canon anymore, look for "Interlude at Darkknell" for the best finding the Death Star plans story ever).

It was the definition of a slow burn, which is one of the reasons the scene where Luthen escapes the Cantwell -class's tractor beams (using a modification on the EU cloak shroud gambit; some of you know what I'm talking about, the rest of you should run to Google or your AI friend and find out) works so well. This scene was typical Star Wars , but it was also one of the only times in the entire first season that we got a scene like this.

One of the complaints you saw a lot during Andor Season One was that it was too slow. Some of those watching it wanted something more akin to the excitement of Rogue One instead of what was more a somber meditation of the effects of fascism on a society. One of the things I've always found so interesting about Star Wars fans is that there are some of them who want the franchise to go all kinds of different directions and there are some who just want lightsabers and starfighters. And here's the thing – the producers of the franchise know that.

There's a world where someone higher up at LucasFilm or Disney stepped in and told Tony Gilroy that he needed to add Darth Vader and about four outer space action scenes. However, they trusted him and let him tell the story his way, leading up to this scene. This is the scene that even the most unabashed Andor haters love because it is everything that you expect from a big space action scene in Star Wars . It reminded people that this was still the galaxy far, far away. It was also was one of the most unique scenes in the show.

There's also a world where the producers demanded this scene was put somewhere closer to the beginning, in order to give viewers that comfortable Star Wars feeling. Thank the Force (which is female, haters) that we didn't get there, because the main reason this scene works so well is this series wasn't typical Star Wars . It was something of a surprise to get a scene like this (as a ship geek, I love the Cantwell ; Imperial design philosophy just does it for me) in the show and that was part of made it work so well. We didn't know what to expect at the beginning of the show; Gilroy and company did a fantastic job of establishing how different Andor was, but this scene reminded us that it was still Star Wars .

Andor has a lot in common with The Acolyte. Both of them are rather well made shows and both of them have a devoted section of the fanbase that hates them with a burning passion (I wouldn't be surprised if they were the same people; Acolyte haters are the kind of people who actually like fascism). Both of them went in different directions than we're used to with their stories and each of them had scenes toward the end that would have made the naysayers happier if they had happened earlier, but would have damaged the show immensely.

Andor was an anti-fascist polemic disguised in Star Wars clothing and that outfit wouldn't be complete without this scene. It was the moment that reminded you that the war against the Empire was, well, a war, one where the smaller side had to use ingenuity to defeat their all-powerful enemies. In a lot of ways, it's the story of Andor in microcosm. Much like the Fondor Haulcraft, the characters of the show have hidden depths and often devastating tricks. While they can't destroy their enemy outright, they can hurt them, turning their own weapons against them. By holding this scene of traditional Star Wars action to the end, Andor 's producers were able to make their show even better, perfectly building to this moment (and, of course, the final episode's amazing funeral scene on Ferrix, a less Star Wars -like action scene that is all the better because this scene preceded it).

What do you think about the fight between Luthen's Haulcraft and the Cantwell ? Is it your favorite Star Wars space action scene or is it the Battle of Ebaq 9 (some of you know, others are Googling)? Sound off in the comment section below.

This year, he took over as the head of the Discovery Campus. In between his busy schedule, Gunathilake caught up with THR to share his vision for the platform and why it is such a key part of the Tallinn sucess formula.

Each year, the Discovery Campus welcomes around 70 emerging professionals and talents, from producers and directors to cinematographers, production designers, composers and production designers, to its workshops and masterclasses.

Gunathilake says it is all about building bridges. And that goes beyond the bridges and networks that socializing and discussing the craft naturally creates. "There is a gap between academia and the film industry," he tells THR . "We thought it is a responsibility of film festivals to help bridge industry and academia and bring them together."

Case in point: Students fresh out of film schools, whether focused on cinematography or other areas, "may have never heard of a sales agent and what they do, they don't know what distribution is and they have never heard of a subject called audience study," he explains. Gunathilake says beyond general education, mentorship is a key focus for him and his team. "It is important to create a platform where mentors are coming – big filmmakers – and emerging talents can present their film and have an exchange with them. They can come together and sit and talk and discuss."

The feedback on these opportunities is strong to enthusiastic. For example, one younger cinematographer from Spain got to spend time with the acclaimed Roberto Schaefer ( Finding Neverland , Monster's Ball , Quantum of Solace ). "She mentioned that she never thought she could sit at a breakfast table and talk about her film with Roberto," Gunathilake tells THR . "And Roberto had seen her film, and then they could talk."

The importance of mentoring is actually captured in the official motto of the Discovery Campus that is featured on its website: "Learn from the mistakes of our mentors, so you don’t have to make them yourself!"

articles.title: Busan-Selected Director Anoop Lokkur Turns His Own Tenant War Into Bengaluru Dark Comedy 'Melgade Mane Kelgade Mane' at India's WAVES Film Bazaar
articles.summary: Indian-Australian filmmaker Anoop Lokkur, whose debut "Don't Tell Mother" premiered at the Busan International Film Festival in 2025, is turning his own standoff with tenants who wouldn't leave his family home into "Melgade Mane Kelgade Mane" (Upstairs Downstairs), a dark comedy in the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar. The Kannada and English-language film follows […]
articles.content:
Indian-Australian filmmaker Anoop Lokkur , whose debut "Don't Tell Mother" premiered at the Busan International Film Festival in 2025, is turning his own standoff with tenants who wouldn't leave his family home into "Melgade Mane Kelgade Mane" (Upstairs Downstairs), a dark comedy in the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar .

The Kannada and English-language film follows Karthik, who returns from Melbourne, along with his wife and young daughter, to look after his ailing father. He expects to take over the top floor of the house in an older Bengaluru neighborhood where his family has lived for three generations. The tenant, government contractor Ramesh, had agreed to move out, then changes his mind. Polite negotiation gives way to a tit-for-tat war as legal routes go nowhere, the power gets cut, property is damaged and access is blocked. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Rosario Dawson Drops First Look at Night Nurse in ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Re-Release as Her Cut Scenes Are Restored Lakers’ Official History Book Gets $9,600 Limited Edition With Magic Johnson Handprints, Staples Center Hardwood and Rare Artwork

Lokkur says that in 2025 he returned to Bangalore with his wife and their 1-year-old daughter, planning to settle upstairs in his parents' home, but the tenants stayed on after their lease ran out and the family ended up crammed into his parents' part of the house. "The whole situation was frustrating and unpleasant. What followed were months of tension, passive aggression and even thinking of ways to get them to vacate. The irony, though, was that only a couple of years earlier, my wife and I had been forced out of a rented home ourselves."

Having been on both sides of the door, he says, he grew curious about ownership, about what it means to call a place home and about how hard people will push to come out on top. "I realized there was a dark comedy in this situation that was universal, and the best way to deal with my frustration was to turn it into a film." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The project is in development, with Lokkur and Mikayla Henke producing through Papunu Films. The budget is $1.3 million, with $156,000 in place, and the team is looking for international co-producers, financiers and sales agents in Goa.

"The film is built like a tennis match. Your sympathies keep switching between the two families, until you're no longer sure who to cheer for," Lokkur says. "I'm interested in how ego quietly takes over and how ordinary decent people justify each small act of revenge until they no longer recognize themselves. It's also a film about Bangalore, a city changing so fast that old neighborhoods and family homes are disappearing."

Henke says she went through the dispute alongside Lokkur, and that with the family living it every day, it was the obvious choice for their next film. "'Don't Tell Mother' was a tender and very personal film. On the surface, 'Melgade Mane Kelgade Mane' (Upstairs Downstairs) might look like the opposite: darker, bolder and funnier. But it comes from the same place, a close eye on family and the things people struggle to say to each other. This time, we just want to take audiences on a much wilder ride."

"Don't Tell Mother" played in the A Window on Asian Cinema section at Busan, was nominated for best youth film at the 2026 Asia Pacific Screen Awards and had its Australian premiere at this year's Sydney Film Festival. Lokkur's short "Long Distance," which Henke produced, screened at the Melbourne International Film Festival and Palm Springs International ShortFest before Canal+ acquired it. Henke was also the first producer on "Don't Tell Mother."

"While it's set in Bengaluru, it's a universal story about housing that people everywhere can relate to and we believe it can travel well beyond India," the producers say.

WAVES Film Bazaar runs as the market component of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

articles.content:
EXCLUSIVE: Hugo Weaving is readying his high-viz jacket for another spell as the The Airport Chaplain . We hear the founders of the production company behind the SBS and Netflix show are pulling together a writing team for Season 2, as they gear up for a busy 2027.

We can reveal Sarinah Masukor, co-writer of Netflix miniseries My Brilliant Career , and Keir Wilkins ( Heartbreak High ) have been brought on as writers for Season 2, which is currently in development at SBS under lead writer and co-creator Elise McCredie.

The Matrix actor Weaving, who plays the title character, first mentioned a second run of the high-rating Australian show in a Hey You Guys podcast in August. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News 'Colin From Accounts' Maker Easy Tiger Adapting Dervla McTiernan Novel 'Three Reasons For Revenge' As TV Series News 'Black Snow': Travis Fimmel Is Back On Cold Case Trail In Teaser For Season 3; Premiere Date Set In Australia

Furthermore, Netflix announced this morning that its Australia and New Zealand service will launch Season 1 on January 25, 2027. What makes this particularly notable is the holdback window for a network original series like The Airport Chaplain in Australia is usually three years, but this will hit streaming in just five months. Wooden Horse co-founder Richard Finlayson confirmed the show is in the works, telling Deadline: "We’re developing a second series with SBS, and the writers are back in the room under Elise McCready’s guidance."

Jude Troy, who launched the Sydney-based Wooden Horse with Finlayson, co-created the show with McCredie. Weaving stars alongside The Pitt breakout Shabana Azeez, Claudia Karvan ( Bump ), Thomas Weatherall ( Heartbreak High ) and Erroll Shand ( All Her Fault ).

The news came in an exclusive interview during which Wooden Horse's bosses also revealed a host of hires, and projects such as the first Australian adaptation of an R.L. Stein book as a TV series, along with co-production developments with the likes of I May Destroy You and Two Weeks in August maker Various Artists Limited and Wild Cards producer. "We have a great team and a lot of different international relationships and collaborations underway," said Finlayson.

The Airport Chaplain has been a breakout hit for Australian multicultural public service broadcaster SBS, achieving its biggest launch of 2026 with 1.7 million tuning in for episode one and streaming records broken. The series broke further records for SBS, reaching 2.4 million viewers on a national total TV basis to date. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Netflix took worldwide rights, as we revealed , and its safe to say it has been one of the most notable new series out of Australia this year.

The eight-part show stars Weaving as as unconventional airport terminal chaplain Tobias Wallace and The Pitt breakout Shabana Azeez as his put-upon boss. The show was inspired by Troy's chance encounter with a Melbourne Airport chaplain, who helped her recover a lost handbag.

Troy pointed to the show's "rounded realism," and noted it "takes some big swings in the stories it deals with, but it does so with a light touch and real humanity," noting that there have been "great responses" from viewers in the U.S., UK and her home country, Ireland, among other territories.

"It speaks to humanity and connects with people," said Troy. "Audiences today are looking for something like that. It is a world and a precinct we all recognise, that we have all travelled through, and it depicts very real people doing very real jobs.

"It is about the lower echelons of the airport and the clash with the upper echelons, and shows a working-class perspective that you don’t often see on Australian television."

Former ABC television chief Finlayson and ex-eOne TV production chief Troy co-founded Wooden Horse with Troy in 2020, as we revealed at the time , and have over the following six years established the company among the leaders in Australia. In a tough market where even the likes of NBCUniversal-backed Matchbox Pictures closed down this year, that's no mean feat.

"We are six years in, and I think we have developed a brand that is known for interesting approaches and stories, strong relationships with the best creators and being a trusted producer," said Finlayson. "Now it is about having the capacity to keep delivering, because we have a lot in development and a number going into production."

Credits include the Logie-winning ABC scripted shows The Clearing and Mother and Son , unscripted series Stuff the British Stole , which is being developed as a TV drama, and Deep North true crime doc series The Cape , and there's about to be a flood of new work hitting the market.

Upcoming is a first children's TV show, live-action drama Emma's Dance Club , which is also noteworthy for its combined TV and movie theater rollout. "The first season has 20 episodes, and we have created five packages, each effectively an hour long," said Finlayson. "Hoyts will release them over the course of the year as family experiences. Hoyts has a large family loyalty club, so it is an interesting way to bring together different release strategies."

We can reveal Wooden Horse has teamed with U.S.-based producer Global Production Studios (GPS) on a screen adaptation of spooky YA stories author R.L. Stine's Dangerous Girls , with Thomas Wilson-White, who wrote episodes of Netflix's Heartbreak High , helming the project.

"This is the first time R.L. Stine has ever been adapted in Australia," said Troy.

She also noted there Wooden Horse has an unnamed co-production with Canada's Blink49 Studios underway, while the heist caper adaptation of Australian unscripted series Stuff the British Stole is now known as Plunder and has UK producer Various Artists Limited aboard, along with Warner Bros. International Television Production Australia, as we revealed in June 2024.

Anchuli Felicia King, who wrote on HBO’s The Sympathizer and The Baby and Deadloch for Prime Video, is the writer and creator. A streamer is circling, we hear. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

Elsewhere, an adaptation of Ashley Collins' Dark Mode with Dan March's Dynamic Television, announced in January 2025, is being set up with an unnamed commissioner, with Safe Home writer Anna Barnes attached. There's also work ongoing to finance The Other Guy star and creator Matt Okine's debut feature film in Queensland. We first flagged development on Being Black n’ Chicken n’ Chips when Wooden Horse launched six years ago.

Wooden Horse has backed up a busy 2026 with series of hires, which we can officially reveal here. Felicity Harrison has joined as the producer's first Head of Commercial and Business Affairs.

She was business affairs chief at Matchbox, which shuttered in February after 18 years in business. At Wooden Horse, she will focus on areas such as legal, business affairs and growing revenues. "We've benefitted from Matchbox's misfortune, as they had such a great team of people," said Finlayson.

Bridget Harvey has become Senior Development Executive, joining from Mr Inbetween and Sunny Nights maker Jungle, and Alexis Talbot Smith ( The Familiars ) joined as a development producer in charge after spells at WildBear and Aquarius Films, with her first job being an associate producer on Emma's Dance Club , on which she led the day-to-day work.

Production and development assistant and coordinator Will Lane has been promoted and Nell O'Grady has been hired from Stranger Than Fiction Films in a similar role. The Other Guy star Okine remains within the company as an exec producer.

Staffing up has been a key part of forward planning for what's gearing up to be a big 2027 for company, which is operating in an Australian creative market that has appeared on the up for several years now.

Finlayson gave a measured assessment of the production sector, noting the strength of local commissioners, who include such as the ABC, SBS, Stan, Binge and Network Seven, and investment from global streamer, who have continued to order originals under the quota system introduced in late 2025 .

"We are well supported by our broadcasters and by local and global streamers, the public broadcasters are relatively well funded, and the Labour government has been supportive. The quotas make a difference, so the local market is in a pretty good place.

"The challenges for Australian producers are much the same as those facing British producers. The U.S. market has changed structurally and is still in a state of flux. We are not seeing it return to pre-COVID levels, so raising the gap is hard for everyone. You have to be well networked internationally and agile when it comes to working with budgets."

Troy addressed how to remain independent in a global production landscape where Banijay Entertainment is now the largest studio outside of the Hollywood big guns, and M&A appears only to apply to those seeking mega-scale. Wooden Horse is owned by its founders, and has investors and board members including Damian Keogh, CEO of theater chain Hoyts, and Peter Allen, former CEO of Scentre Group and current Chairman of Coles.

"There are always conversations, and the rumour mill is always active," she said. "Fully independent Australian companies have shown how agile they can be. That flexibility matters. Not being tethered to one mothership is probably how we have continued to get projects made."

articles.title: Australian Brothers Discover They Are Indian Cinema Royalty in WAVES Film Bazaar Documentary 'Dada & Us'
articles.summary: Three Melbourne brothers who grew up believing they were German, then learned their grandfather founded Bombay Talkies, are at the center of "Dada & Us," filmmaker Anupam Sharma's documentary in the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar. The project is one of five in the market's new documentary strand. Walter, Peter and Paul Dietze traced […]
articles.content:
Three Melbourne brothers who grew up believing they were German, then learned their grandfather founded Bombay Talkies, are at the center of "Dada & Us," filmmaker Anupam Sharma 's documentary in the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar .

The project is one of five in the market's new documentary strand. Walter, Peter and Paul Dietze traced their lineage to Himansu Rai after finding a photograph in an attic. Rai's studio was later run by Devika Rani , who was the first person to receive the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, India's highest film honor. She steered Bombay Talkies through World War II after being widowed at 32, and launched the screen careers of Ashok Kumar, Dilip Kumar and Madhubala. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Sundance-Winning 'Cactus Pears' Producer's Delhi Beauty Salon Comedy-Drama 'Nisa' Bows at India's WAVES Film Bazaar New 'Serendipity' Movie Casts Auli‘i Cravalho (EXCLUSIVE)

The brothers keep more than 3,000 of her letters, photos and studio documents in a spare room of a suburban Melbourne house, among them some 1,100 items of correspondence from her five years running the studio. Sharma says Peter Dietze was introduced to him by the film's executive producer Vikrant Kishore, a Melbourne film academic, and that as someone hooked on Indian film history since making his documentary "Brand Bollywood Downunder," he lit up at the chance to handle material from before India was India. "The largest surviving body of her own writing is in suburban Melbourne, and almost nobody in India knows it's there. Once you know that, you don't get to un-know it."

Back in India, her jewelry, personal belongings and surviving Roerich paintings have been locked in a Bengaluru government strongroom as evidence since 1994. The state took over her Tataguni estate in 1996, promising a museum that has yet to materialize. The documentary runs a parallel narrative following a court case over the inheritance of her memorabilia, which is nearing a conclusion. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Sharma says the film is not a history lesson, and that he is not preaching. "I want India to know about this amazing star, a creative woman, a business woman running a studio through a war," he says, adding that he also wants Australian audiences to see it as their story.

The project is in late development. The treatment, built with the family's own notes, is in its third draft, the archive has been cataloged and priority digitization of the correspondence from 1940 to 1945 is under way. Sharma is filming with the lawyers in Bengaluru next week, with the main shoot across Australia and India starting in 2027.

Sharma's Temple is producing with the Dietze family. The budget is $1.2 million, with $800,000 in place, and a commitment for theatrical distribution in Australia, New Zealand and Canada makes the film eligible for a 40% producer offset. Screen NSW gave producer Farabee Kabir a travel grant to attend the Bazaar.

The producers say access was the first reason they backed the film, since the Dietze family has given them both the archive and themselves, and nobody else can make it. "Timing: the Australia–India co-production treaty has been in force since November 2023 and is conspicuously under-used – a story that is literally half-Australian and half-Indian by blood is close to an ideal demonstration of what that treaty was signed for. And the clock: our three principals are in their sixties and seventies, and the material they're holding is paper, in a house, with no institution behind it. The case for making this now makes itself."

In Goa, the team wants an Indian co-producer with documentary and archival experience and a real creative role, an archival and restoration partner such as the Film Heritage Foundation, the National Film Archive or NFDC, and an Indian broadcaster or streamer. "Devika Rani is not a niche subject in India, she's a foundational one," the producers say.

Sharma has spent 25 years working between the Indian and Australian film industries. Temple has worked on more than 400 projects, including "Dil Chahta Hai," "Salaam Namaste" and "Heyy Babyy," and Sharma directed the feature "UnIndian," starring Brett Lee and Tannishtha Chatterjee. "Brand Bollywood Downunder" streams on Netflix in Australia and New Zealand and won best documentary at the U.K. Asian Film Festival in London. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

He is finishing "Framed," a film about Islamophobia told through what he calls Australia's biggest terrorism bungle, and has development investment from Screen Australia for a dark comedy about an Indian doctor in Western Australia. In January he goes into pre-production in Victoria on his thriller "Durga," with producers Cathy Rodda and Jannine Barnes and major cast from mainstream Indian cinema.

WAVES Film Bazaar runs as the market component of the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

articles.title: Berlinale Forum-Selected Director R. Gowtham Salutes Village Health Workers in Tamil Dark Comedy 'Superman Vivagaram' at India's WAVES Film Bazaar
articles.summary: Tamil filmmaker R. articles.content:
Tamil filmmaker R. Gowtham , whose debut "Members of the Problematic Family" premiered in the Berlinale's Forum section and won the Young Cinema Award at the Asia Pacific Screen Awards this year, is bringing his dark comedy " Superman Vivagaram " (Superman Issue) to the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar .

Set in the village of Koovathur in Tamil Nadu, the film centers on Jolly, an orphan trying to revive a decade-old program to prevent non-communicable diseases. He goes from house to house checking on patients, runs his operation from a desk under a solitary tree and squares off against Raja Doctor, an illegal quack whose practice draws more patients than the government doctors. At home, his pregnant wife Divya is turning against the village. In the field, he relies on Kannagi, who heads the team of community health workers, until his plan to bring in a payment model turns the staff against him. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘La Bola Negra’ Wins Audience Award at London Film Festival Martin Scorsese Says His 'Cleopatra' Movie With Angelina Jolie Was 'Ruined' by Seth Rogen and the Sony Hack: 'It Was Gonna Be Really Wild'

Gowtham says "Superman Vivagaram" is also the first script he wrote, and that it grew out of his own decade as a rural health program manager working with community health workers who covered hundreds of villages in Chengalpattu district. "The film is the ode to Kannagi, our field supervisor who led the team of frontline workers who walked hundreds of miles visiting the homes of the beneficiaries and checking on their health. You cannot imagine us roaming the streets of the villages like that 10 years back. It's an herculean task, but we are fictionalizing those experiences to the contemporary decade, happening right now, with lots of fictional elements added to it." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Casting is complete and the technical crew is in place, and Gowtham says the project is moving from early development into development. The budget is $150,000, with $37,500 in place. Tamilarasan Kalidass of Labyrinth Narratives and Mukesh Subramaniam of Potato Eaters Collective, who produced Gowtham's debut, are producing again. The team is looking for co-producers, financiers, post-production partners, sales agents, distributors and festival programmers in Goa, and Gowtham says they will also "explore international creative collaboration with this project."

A published poet in Tamil, Gowtham has translated the work of Lydia Davis, Alejandro Jodorowsky and Amol Palekar into the language. He headed content for TV channel Zee Tamil and for the digital outlet Asiaville Tamil, and his documentary "On the Trails of Aandi" was selected for the Vancouver Asian Film Festival in 2023. "Members of the Problematic Family" is also in the international competition at this year's International Film Festival of Kerala.

"I believe every reasonable adult in the globe is my audience," Gowtham says. "I don't have the intention to convey anything specifically to them, but I am planning to thematically discuss with them, why preventive health measures do not have takers anywhere? Why do community organizations exist? What's the role of outsiders in poverty alleviation? Why do we want to take care of others? What is philanthropy? Why do we need super heroes?"

The producers say that having been friends with Gowtham for many years gave them the trust to begin a film, and that as the work went on it was professional ethics and commitment that held the friendship together. "We know Gowtham's commitment to the society, we believe as a producer it is our responsibility to protect the director's vision, we know how much value this project brings to the current chaotic world, we felt it's our responsibility to back it."

Gowtham is also distributing "Members of the Problematic Family," and has written another script, about mental health, that he plans to make "with bare hands." He is also shooting a documentary about the rivers and buffaloes of Chennai.

"Film Bazaar has given us the community which we were longing for a long time," the producers say. They add that meeting fellow young filmmakers and international producers, sales agents and programmers gives young producers like them hope and confidence. "We always felt Film Bazaar is the platform for like minded collaborators who can nurture each other to become a set of conscience keepers who practice cinema." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.content:
Jennifer Lawrence thinks a bow and arrow she received after appearing on The Hunger Games may have been stolen from her.

The Oscar winner appeared on Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen on Thursday night alongside Josh Hutcherson , marking their first joint interview in over 10 years. The appearance was tied to the release of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , the prequel film where they reprise their respective roles of Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

articles.content:
Jorrybell Agoto , the lead actress of Rafael Manuel 's " Filipinana ," the Philippines' submission for the international feature Oscar, died on Nov. 17 after a battle with lymphoma. She was 32.

Her brother Jed Agoto told GMA News Online that she died at 5:20 p.m. local time. Epicmedia, the production company behind the film, announced the news on Instagram on Nov. 19 alongside a monochrome photo of the actress. "We love you, Belle. No more pain," the company wrote. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories ‘La Bola Negra’ Wins Audience Award at London Film Festival Martin Scorsese Says His 'Cleopatra' Movie With Angelina Jolie Was 'Ruined' by Seth Rogen and the Sony Hack: 'It Was Gonna Be Really Wild'

Agoto was moved into the critical care unit of St. Luke's Medical Center in the Philippines in September. Those close to her then turned to social media to raise money for her medical bills. Her brother said in October that three tumors had been detected in her left lung. The family also asked President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his relatives for support, pointing to a shared hometown: Sarrat, in Ilocos Norte province.

Her character in "Filipiñana," Isabel, is a 17-year-old who works as a tee girl at a members-only golf club. Agoto first played her in Manuel's 2020 short of the same name, which won the Silver Bear Jury Prize at the Berlinale, and returned to the part for his feature debut. The feature premiered in the World Cinema Dramatic Competition at Sundance in January, where it won the Special Jury Award for Creative Vision, before its European premiere in the Berlinale's Perspectives section in February. Kino Lorber picked up North American rights. Jia Zhangke executive produced.

"The world has just lost one of its brightest stars. We have just lost a great friend. Producers Bianca Balbuena and Bradley Liew said they were devastated by the news. "Not only is she the face of 'Filipinana' but more than that, she is our friend, our sister, our beloved Jorrybell, ever so funny and kind, sweet and loving. We love her," they said.

Before "Filipinana," Agoto worked mostly on the indie and stage circuit, including Virgin Labfest. Gian Arre's "Tether" and Kevin Mayuga's "When This Is All Over," both in the 2023 Cinemalaya lineup, featured her, and the latter brought her a Gawad Urian nomination for best supporting actress. articles.title: 'Sh*t Happens' Is Full of Dark Humor, But Its Director Knows It Will Cause a Stink in the DR
articles.summary: José María Cabral, who has seen three of his films submitted for the Oscars, just premiered his new feature at Tallinn – and there is more to it than it might seem to folks outside his home country.
articles.content:
José María Cabral has seen three of his films submitted for the best international feature film Oscar race by the Dominican Republic, namely The Projectionist , Woodpeckers , and Checkmate . That means that you can probably trust his gut when it comes to picking themes that are cinematic and feature more than a trickle of ideas. So, why did he just celebrate the world premiere of his newest film that is not only a black comedy but also has the ominous title Sh*t Happens ? Cue the toilet humor, you say? Well, let's first flush away any doubt you may have that this writer just made all this stuff up. The film did indeed premiere Thursday night in the Official Competition of the 30th edition of Estonia's Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF). And here is what it is about: The young daughter of a wealthy couple suffers from gut issues that the doctors just can't seem to heal. The young nanny Lidi, portrayed by Cindy Galán, remains her upbeat self though, making the little girl smile despite all the health worries. And maid Dominga (Isabel Spencer) handles cooking and cleaning, sharing a small bunk bed with Lidi. Related Stories Movies "I'm in Preparation for the End of Our World": Golshifteh Farahani on Art, War and Her Tallinn Premiere Movies IDFA: 'The Year of the Ghost' and 'Memories of Lightning' Win Amsterdam Doc Fest Awards

Father Raúl, played by Fele Martínez, a frustrated biotechnologist, keeps experimenting with homemade cures – and one day, he finds what seems to be the "miracle cure." But trust us, you don't want to know what it is made of! Neither does his wife Verónica, played by Lizbeth Santos – initially. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But soon, it seems that the household's various issues and struggles begin to disappear. But you can likely smell that the miracle eventually ends up taking an unexpected turn. The various people in the household even end up playing a very different game of thrones, so to speak.

Cabral, Galán, Santos and production designer Mónica de Moya took some audience questions after the premiere, and the director shared insight into the Upstairs-Downstairs dynamics portrayed in the film.

"There's something about shit that is very democratic," Cabral said. "Everybody shits. Poor people shit. Rich people shit. So, in a way, using it as a resource is a very absurd idea." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

But he highlighted that viewers back home in the Dominican Republic will immediately react to the Spanish title of the movie – Comemierda , or "shit-eater."

"This is also, in my country, something that people aspire to be because it's something about power and class," Cabral explained. "It sounds ironic, but people actually go, 'I'm a shit-eater!' or 'I want to be a shit-eater.' 'I go to fine restaurants – I'm a shit-eater.' 'I have a yacht. I have a big house.' So even the title is playing with the audience."

Added the director: "Whenever we show the film, if people see the political side, the social side of the movie, of course, they laugh, but then they question, 'What are we laughing at?' That's the principal objective of making this movie and trying to treat the characters principally very seriously, because they are not in a comedy because they are actually living in the drama." And Cabral concluded: "It's going to upset people back home, let me tell you that. It's going to upset some people." After all, "we are questioning privilege. … Just with the title, people are going to react. They are going to be like, 'Why are you pointing at us? Why are you pointing the camera at this place?' The movie is questioning it, and it's putting it in an absurd situation, and it's pointing out the inequalities, the hierarchies, and it's doing it in a fun, entertaining way - and that bothers people."

articles.title: Invincible Season 5 First Trailer Just Apologized to Fans for Season 4's Weirdest Episode

This takes place in the beloved Burger Mart booth, and this is a way to catch people up on last season and tease what is to come. However, this time around, the trailer doesn't have Mark Grayson […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The new Invincible Season 5 teaser has hit, and it is very similar to past teasers for the show. This takes place in the beloved Burger Mart booth, and this is a way to catch people up on last season and tease what is to come. However, this time around, the trailer doesn't have Mark Grayson talking to Atom Eve or his boss, Cecil. Instead, this time around, he is sitting across from Damien Darkblood. Not only that, but Mark is not happy, and he really doesn't want to talk about anything except for the fact that Damien interrupted last season for a side quest that made a lot of fans mad.

In the Invincible Season 5 teaser , Mark mentions how two of his friends were lost in another dimension and Atom Eve was struggling with her powers. He then tore into Damien Darkblood about summoning him into Hell for a side quest that he didn't care about, and that didn't mean anything in the grand scheme of things. It is the same complaint that fans had about that specific episode last season.

Invincible Promises No More Side Quests Image Courtesy of Prime Video Now, to be honest, while a lot of fans were mad that the episode in Hell slowed down the momentum leading to the Viltrumite War , it was a fun episode. In this teaser, Mark even mentioned as much when he talked about how cool Satan was, which is obvious since Bruce Campbell voiced him. However, as fun as it was, and as great as it was to hear Campbell voicing anyone on Invincible, it did slow things down, and this teaser gave the show a chance to apologize for it and promise it wouldn't happen again.

Of course, this was done by having Mark make Damien promise he wouldn't summon him for any more side quests. While Damien tried to emphasize this was for character building, he did make a promise of sorts. He "demon promised," which really didn't make Mark feel any more secure in it, since he didn't know what "demon promised" meant. However, in the end, this was a way to "demon promise" the audience that Season 5 wouldn't have another side quest that interrupted the story's pacing. However, the question now remains what the story will include, and there were some things in the teaser that hinted at it.

For one thing, there were Viltrumites in disguise in the diner, including Kregg, Anissa, and Lucan in human clothes. This clearly hints at their continued assimilation and presence on Earth. The conversation between Mark and Damien also opened up a lot of hints. Amanda and Robot are still trapped in the Flaxan Dimension, so they need to be rescued or find a way back home. This should also mark the beginning of the period that leads Robot into becoming a major threat, as he did in the comics. Damien is also working on a script, which has some Easter eggs too, including the introduction of Jack Quaid's character , Gravitator. There is also a drawing of Dinosaurus, which should lead to him showing up this season.

The project evolved out of a documentary exploration of the world Alqadar grew up in. The feature screenplay was developed at the Writers Ink Screenwriting Lab in 2023, where it won the Emerging Voice in Indian Cinema Award, and was selected for TorinoFilmLab's Next Feature Film program in 2026. Alqadar's proof-of-concept short "Stray Girls" tested the film's tone and visual language in the Delhi neighborhood where she intends to shoot. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Martin Scorsese Says His 'Cleopatra' Movie With Angelina Jolie Was 'Ruined' by Seth Rogen and the Sony Hack: 'It Was Gonna Be Really Wild' ‘La Bola Negra’ Wins Audience Award at London Film Festival

"Nisa" follows 24-year-old Fiza, who returns to her mother's home in Delhi after an abrupt divorce, only to find that her old bedroom is being prepared for her brother's wedding. She reluctantly works at her mother's beauty salon. Amid botched wax jobs, gossip and driving lessons, Fiza begins to imagine a life she can choose for herself.

"As a child, my mother's beauty salon in New Delhi was one of my favorite places. I remember women arriving in burqas and leaving with freshly colored hair. I loved their humor and their ease around one another. Years later, when I returned, I questioned if home could be a place of return. Fiza's story grew out of those two experiences," Alqadar says.

The project is in development, with filming planned for December 2027 and January 2028. Neeraj Churi is producing through Lotus Visual Productions in the U.K., alongside Eugene Sun Park of Chicago's Full Spectrum Features and Mumbai-based Khan & Kumar Media, which partners with New York's Ammi Media.

Churi has produced Sundance winner " Cactus Pears " and SXSW Audience Award winner "A Place of Our Own." He is also executive producer on "Lovers in the Blue Night" (Netpac Award, Venice 2026).

"The script was a page-turner and certain images stayed with me long after I'd finished reading," Churi says. "Ambarien writes from lived experience, and you feel it in her affection for these women and her eye for the absurd in their everyday lives. Working with her on 'Stray Girls' made me want to help her bring that same sensibility to a feature and find audiences for it in India and internationally."

Now living without papers in northeastern India, Aliya and her family struggle to survive and find a place to belong. As their circumstances deteriorate, she finds solace in nature. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories AI Vocal Modifier Voicemod Inks Disney Deal to Add Star Wars, Marvel Soundboards to Platform Disney Quarterly Revenue Rises 16% and Profit Doubles; Company Forecasts $3 Billion in Annual Cost Savings by 2029 Including Through Layoffs

"I keep coming back to ordinary people nobody listens to. Climate change is pushing families out of their homes, and the suffering does not stop at the border. I wanted to show that through a child who can't speak but notices everything. Aliya wants to be a tree because trees have roots and nobody asks where they're from," Morchhale tells Variety .

Morchhale's previous films include "Walking With the Wind" (2017), "Widow of Silence" (2018) and "White Snow" (2025). His upcoming projects include "Floating Flowers," about an Indian man and a 6-year-old American girl stranded at sea during the 2004 tsunami.

It is still early days. The film is in the initial phase of development and creative work has yet to begin. Neither company has attached a director or cast, and those details will be revealed at a later date.

"Maharaja Ranjit Singh Ji's life and legacy offer an extraordinary canvas for cinematic storytelling. His journey, leadership and contribution to history deserve to be presented in a manner that does justice to his stature. Through this collaboration with B4 Makers Studios, we aim to create a truly grand theatrical experience that brings this remarkable chapter of history to audiences in a powerful and memorable way," said Shibasish Sarkar, founder of Katha Studios.

Yadwinder Deep Singh, founder and designated partner of B4 Makers Studios, said the company was proud to be attached to a story of such weight and inspiration. "His legacy is deeply rooted in courage, vision and leadership. Ranjit Singh founded the Sikh Empire and ruled it from Lahore for close to four decades until his death in 1839. His story has so far played out mostly on television. Actor-politician Raj Babbar's "Maharaja Ranjit Singh" ran on public broadcaster Doordarshan from 2010 to 2011, while Contiloe Pictures' "Sher-e-Punjab: Maharaja Ranjit Singh," with Damanpreet Singh in the title role, aired on Life OK in 2017. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: What Happened to Face/Off 2? John Travolta Reveals Why He Turned Down Highly Anticipated Sequel
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Paramount One of the best action movies of the 1990s was the John Woo sci-fi thriller Face/Off. The movie stars John Travolta as an FBI agent named Sean Archer who has been trying to bring in a master criminal named Castor Troy for years. Nicolas Cage plays Castor Troy in one of his more over-the-top and […]
articles.content:
Add Us On Google One of the best action movies of the 1990s was the John Woo sci-fi thriller Face/Off . The movie stars John Travolta as an FBI agent named Sean Archer who has been trying to bring in a master criminal named Castor Troy for years. Nicolas Cage plays Castor Troy in one of his more over-the-top and manic performances. However, the big twist that played into the movie's title was that Castor ended up in a coma, and Archer underwent a procedure that had Castor's face removed and placed on him so he could figure out where a bomb was planted. When Castor woke up, he realized what happened and forced the scientists to put Archer's face on him, and the two actors play each other's characters for the rest of the movie.

In an interview with Collider , Travolta explained why the rumored Face/Off sequel has never gotten made, and he said it was all because the scripts sent to him were never right. "The two scripts that they sent me, they did not get it right," Travolta said. "And it was amazing how they missed the premise… The people involved loved the movie so much, but they didn't understand why it worked and why the sequel would have to have the same elements to make it work."

John Travolta Explains What He Needs From a Face/Off Sequel Image Courtesy of Paramount According to Travolta, the one thing that made Face/Off such a great movie wasn't the sci-fi premise or the action scenes. What made it work so well was that he was playing Nicolas Cage and Cage was playing John Travolta. He said that he was always worried that they were not getting it right, but that Cage was comfortable with what they were doing the entire time. He said they watched dailies to make sure it was working, and it ended up paying off. Travolta said the whole reason the movie succeeded was that they were playing each other.

However, when it comes to the Face/Off sequel scripts that were sent to him, that entire aspect was ignored. He said the humor and the magic came from him and Cage playing each other, using each other's mannerisms and copying the way they move and speak. He said that the entire gimmick that let him have fun making the movie was the body swap, and that was something that was missing from both scripts he was sent.

At the same time, a Face/Off sequel is going to be a hard sell to Travolta anyway because he doesn't like sequels. He thought back and said that he didn't appear in many sequels, but he did mention the ones he actually enjoyed were the Elmore Leonard adaptations, Get Shorty and Be Cool . However, he said that Be Cool was a lot easier to make as a sequel since it was a comedy, while making a sequel to a dramatic movie is a lot harder to get right.

Do you wish that there was a Face/Off sequel, or do yoy agree with John Travolta's reasons for not wanting to make it the way the scripts were presented to him? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

" Project 11 ," a 2011 survival thriller made by 11 directors working remotely from 11 cities, will be re-released Nov. 26 as the first title under Oh Short Flips ' new Classic Shorts vertical.

The short pits 11 gamers in 11 cities against one another. Each has 11 minutes to live, and only the final survivor wins. Made years before online phenomena such as the Blue Whale Challenge caused alarm worldwide, the film dealt with fears around deadly real-world gaming dares. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Jennifer Lawrence Says 'Absolutely F---ing Not' to Transforming Into X-Men's Mystique Again 'X-Men': 'Hunger Games' Actor Ben Wang Circling Iceman Role in Marvel's Reboot

Mumbai-based filmmaker Vikas Chandra drove the project, spending months finding 11 directors willing to take part. Their combined crews numbered around 100 people, spread across New York, Los Angeles, Toronto, London, Luxembourg, Tel Aviv, Dar es Salaam, Balochistan, Mumbai, Beijing and Tokyo.

The directors could not meet in person. All pre-production and storyboarding happened online. To make actors on different continents look as though they shared a frame, the filmmakers matched eyelines, faked over-the-shoulder setups and found lookalike locations in cities such as London and New York, then tied the footage together through lighting, lens choices and choreography.

The film went from script to finished cut in 149 days. A first version running 25 minutes was trimmed to 11 minutes and 11 seconds.

Alongside Chandra (Mumbai), the directors are Alessio Giorgetti (New York), Ali Ahmed Brohi (Balochistan), Dharamveer Singh Chauhan (Luxembourg), Ikematsu Hiro (Tokyo), Joseph Cohen (Tel Aviv), Nkumi Mtingwa (Dar es Salaam), Rafal Rakoczy (London), Ryan Singh (Toronto), Sydney Walsh (Los Angeles) and Yi Luo (Beijing). blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

"Long before the AI times, we made 'Project 11' with pure HumInt (Human Intelligence) – one part madness, one part ingenuity and a lot of passion, just like the write-ups called it back then," Chandra said. "Eleven filmmakers from eleven cities who had mostly never met, connecting over late-night Skype calls, putting serious faith in strangers, and somehow scrambling crew, locations and equipment on a shoestring to pull off one crazy lab experiment in filmmaking."

Classic Shorts will bring back well-regarded short films from earlier years that are now hard to come by, aimed at today's online audiences.

Producer Ranjan Singh, founder of Oh Short Flips, said six months of releasing shorts on the company's channel had shown that well-made stories always find an audience. "And we know there are so many classic shorts that are good but not available anywhere for the audience. When we did some inquiries, we realized so many filmmakers would like to release their earlier shorts for the audience to watch. Thus, we've decided to release these Classic Shorts also on Oh Short Flips."

Singh added that the team made the film on a basic understanding of collaboration. "Even back then when social media wasn't that popular we found these directors who wanted to tell a story together. Vikas led from the front and ensured the entire process was smooth and coherent. I am extremely proud that we're starting our Classic Shorts section with 'Project 11.'"

Chandra said that, looking back, the film was probably a little ahead of its moment. "It feels good that the film is getting another life now, on a channel dedicated to shorts."

The news was unveiled on the sidelines of the WAVES Film Bazaar , the market arm of the International Film Festival of India in Goa.

The odds look to be in favor of the Hunger Games franchise, as it is likely to gobble up a box office debut on the level of its impressive hits from more than a decade ago.

Lionsgate releases The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping in 3,900 North American theaters on Friday, with the studio projecting it to gross north of $80 million domestically. However, sources expect that the film will actually open much higher, likely surpassing $100 million and potentially reaching upwards of $130 million. Sunrise on the Reaping takes place in Panem on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Hunger Games, 24 years before the events in The Hunger Games , the initial novel that published in 2008. The franchise's first five movies have surpassed $3.3 billion at the worldwide box office, with the initial four films led by Lawrence as Katniss, Josh Hutcherson as Peeta and Liam Hemsworth as Gale.

With its box office opening, the latest movie is expected to mark a significant uptick over that of 2023's The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes . That prequel film featured Tom Blyth as the young Coriolanus Snow — the villainous character played by Fiennes in Sunrise on the Reaping — alongside Rachel Zegler and Hunter Schafer. The Ballad of Songbirds & Snakes opened to a disappointing $44 million domestically before ending its run with $166.4 million domestically and a global sum of $361.8 million. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

The fan took footage from different Marvel movies and Disney+ shows and added trailer footage to explain what is happening in the upcoming movie and how it all ties into past moments. This is a big deal because one of the biggest complaints of casual fans is that Marvel movies require too much homework to keep up. However, those fans are offset by others who demand that everything be tied together, or the movies that stand alone won't matter.

This fan-made trailer on BPM Editz does a great job of doing the homework for viewers. This allows the trailer to be all anyone needs to understand what Doctor Doom is doing and how it ties into everyone in the MCU.

The Avengers: Doomsday Video Is a Perfect Explainer Image Courtesy of Marvel This fan-made video does everything anyone w ould need to catch up before Avengers: Doomsday . It all starts with the moment from Avengers: Endgame where Captain America was supposed to go through time to return all the Infinity Stones. Of course, Steve never returned and chose to live a secret life with Peggy Carter. However, it then switches over to the end of the Loki series. This is a big deal because there are a lot of movie fans who refuse to watch the Disney+ shows, even though many of them are better in just about every way than the recent Marvel movies. The Loki show in particular was a fantastic watch and revealed that the end is coming. It also showed Loki holding all the timelines together as best he can.

Avengers: Endgame Encore showed Loki going to visit Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter in the past. He said he was there to help them, and showing Loki holding the timelines together reveals why he had to visit Steve and Peggy. There were then the final moments from Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania where Scott Lang was worrying that something was coming based on what Kang told him. While the movie was panned and Kang was mostly removed from the MCU, the moments with Kang were still huge moments that foreshadowed Avengers: Doomsday .

This was followed by Kang talking about seeing how it all ended, which once again hinted at what Doctor Doom has planned. Up next was the TVA post-credit scene from Avengers: Endgame Encore , which revealed countless Earths were dying in rapid succession. To explain this, there was a scene with Kang talking to Loki, a clip of Doctor Strange telling Spider-Man about the multiverse in Spider-Man: No Way Home , and the moment that Strange and Spider-Man accidentally opened a portal on Earth-616.

After this was Monica Rambeau ending up in the X-Men universe with Beast in The Marvels , immediately followed by Reed Richards on Earth-838 explaining to Doctor Strange how incursions happen in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness . Finally, there was a look at Doctor Doom from the Avengers: Doomsday trailers, along with a few of the people he has collected, including Hulk and Scarlet Witch . Honestly, even without rewatching any of the movies or streaming shows, this fan-made trailer is all they need to be caught up for the next giant MCU event.

articles.title: 5 Perfect Steven Universe Episodes That Define the Whole Show, Including the One That Cancelled It
articles.summary: Courtesy of Cartoon Network Steven Universe premiered on Cartoon Network in November 2013. The hit five-season series came to an end in January 2019, after 160 episodes. It was followed by Steven Universe: The Movie in September and the epilogue series Steven Universe Future from December 2019 to March 2020. Steven Universe followed the adventures of its half-human, half-Gem (an […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Steven Universe premiered on Cartoon Network in November 2013. The hit five-season series came to an end in January 2019, after 160 episodes. It was followed by Steven Universe: The Movie in September and the epilogue series Steven Universe Future from December 2019 to March 2020. Steven Universe followed the adventures of its half-human, half-Gem (an alien race) titular character. The Gems invaded Earth thousands of years ago and fought a civil war that ended with the corruption of all Gems left on the planet, except for the select few protected by Rose Quartz, Steven's mother. Through the course of the series, viewers watched as Steven came into his powers and fought the Homeworld Gems that sought to destroy them and the planet. It was a spectacular show, and there are five perfect episodes that truly define it.

"Jailbreak" was the 52nd and final episode of Steven Universe 's first season. In the previous episode, a team of Gems from Homeworld traveled to Earth and captured the Crystal Gems, which were Steven (Zach Callison), Pearl (Deedee Magno Hall), Amethyst (Michaela Dietz), and Garnet (Estelle). They were placed aboard their ship and began heading into space. Being half human, Steven was able to escape from his cell and free Ruby (Lo Mutuc) (Erica Luttrell), a Gem he had never met before. He then went with her to locate Sapphire (Erica Luttrell), who could be heard singing. He freed her, and the two reunited, forming into Garnet and revealing her to be a fusion. Steven then ran off to rescue Pearl and Amethyst and take control of the ship from Peridot (Shelby Rabara) while Garnet fought Jasper (Kimberly Brooks).

Their battle destroyed the ship's engine and sent it crashing back to Earth. Lapis Lazuli (Jennifer Paz) then tricked Jasper into fusing with her and dragged her down to the bottom of the ocean as revenge for her imprisonment. "Jailbreak" is one of the most iconic episodes of Steven Universe . The major reveal of Garnet being a fusion is a big part of that. Garnet was a fusion born from the romantic love of Ruby and Sapphire. While fighting Jasper, she sang "Stronger Than You." Its message was that Garnet will always be stronger than Jasper because she is made of love, and it was paired with an epic battle cooler than any that had been in the show so far, and there had been some truly great ones. The song is also the most well-known of the series and is a favorite of many fans, which boosts the episode's status.

4.) "The Answer" Season two episode 22 was "The Answer." Building off of the big reveal in "Jailbreak," the episode tells Garnet's backstory. In that episode, Garnet mentioned they were waiting to tell Steven she was a fusion until his birthday. This episode takes place on that day, and instead of revealing that she is a fusion, Garnet told the story of how she became one. 5.750 years prior, Sapphire was an aristocrat assigned to Blue Diamond's court, one of the four rulers of all Gem-kind. Ruby was assigned to protect Sapphire. After Rose Quartz (Susan Egan) and Pearl launched an attack against them, Ruby leapt to protect Sapphire, and they inadvertently fused. This was seen as blasphemous by the other Homeworld Gems, and the now unfused pair ended up falling from the Cloud Arena.

From then on, they were to be stranded on Earth, never able to return to Homeworld because of what they had done. So they resigned themselves to their new life and would live it together. They discussed that and their experience through the song "Something Entirely New," which pulled some melodic inspiration from "Stronger Than You." At the end, they danced and fused back into Garnet, who then fell down a hill and landed by Pearl and Rose, who recognized them. She started asking them questions about who she is and such, with Rose saying she already knows the answer: love. This episode made the list because of the depth it provided to Garnet's story, a character known for being quite mysterious, as well as its unmistakable portrayal of a same-sex relationship when that was still considered relatively taboo in children's entertainment at the time. This actually caused the episode to be banned in Russia and Bulgaria, something Cartoon Network wasn't happy about.

3.) "Bismuth" "Bismuth" was episodes 20 and 21 of season three. Steven went into the pocket dimension within the mane of his magical pet Lion to store something, and in doing so he accidentally popped a bubbled Gem. She reformed, and Steven brought her out of the mane, where Pearl and Garnet were excited to see her. It was Bismuth (Uzo Aduba), a Crystal Gem thought to have been lost during the war. That was not true, though. She had been poofed by Rose following an argument. Bismuth was the blacksmith for the rebellion and had made a weapon called the Breaking Point, which was capable of shattering Gems. She showed it to Rose, who was dead set against the idea. Bismuth refused to let it go, so Rose poofed her. Her Gem was placed in Lion's mane, and Rose lied about what happened to her.

Bismuth showed the Breaking Point to Steven, who held the same opinion about shattering. They fought, and Bismuth began to think Steven truly was Rose and not someone new. He nearly lost, but thankfully he had Rose's sword with him and was able to poof and bubble her, just as his mother had. Injured, he limped back to the house where he told the Gems the real story about what had happened thousands of years prior, and she was placed in the bubble room. This double-length episode was perfect for multiple reasons. The battle between Steven and Bismuth was very well done, both in animation and stakes. They provided a lot of depth to her and added more backstory for Rose. Her sword also had more lore built up that would be relevant later, when the audience learned the true story of what happened to Pink Diamond in "A Single Pale Rose."

2.) "Reunited" "Reunited" was episodes 23 and 24 of season five. The episode began with "For Just One Day Let's Only Think About (Love)," a song about putting aside all of the horrible things that had happened in the past few years aside and just focusing on the love shared by Ruby and Sapphire. The first part of the episode was all about their wedding , which was reportedly the first same-sex engagement and wedding in a cartoon. This is also what got Steven Universe cancelled. Many countries were against Ruby and Sapphire being in a same-sex relationship, and multiple episodes had faced censorship because of it. The wedding, which series creator Rebecca Sugar fought hard for, caused some funding to be pulled so Cartoon Network pulled the plug. Regardless, it was a beautiful and touching ceremony officiated, of course, by Steven. At the end, Ruby and Sapphire became Garnet once again following their separation in episodes prior, an incredibly satisfying moment after all that had transpired.

The second half of the episode saw Blue Diamond (Lisa Hannigan) and Yellow Diamond (Patti Lupone) crashed the party, literally, as they attacked during the wedding reception. They used their arm ships to awaken The Cluster, a dangerous bubbled cluster of Gem shards at Earth's core, in the hopes it would destroy Earth, but instead it attacked Yellow Diamond's ship and then returned to sleep after disabling it. The Crystal Gems engaged the Diamonds in battle, greatly outmatched by their supreme power. It took Steven using his mother's pink aura, which they recognized, for them to finally stop fighting and recognize Steven for who he truly was. Well, mostly. They still called him Pink Diamond instead of Steven, but it was progress. Between the beautiful wedding and the epic battle against Blue and Yellow by every Crystal Gem including Bismuth, "Reunited" is easily one of the most perfect and best episodes of the series and very worthy of being on this list.

1.) "Change Your Mind" "Change Your Mind" was the series finale of Steven Universe , occupying episodes 29 through 32 of season five, making it the longest episode of the series at 44 minutes. Blue Diamond broke Steven and his friends out of prison on Homeworld. When Yellow Diamond caught her, the two got into a fight unlike any seen prior in the series given their sheer size and power. Steven was able to make her realize the mental abuse White Diamond (Christine Ebersole) had put her through, and they both endeavored to get the Crystal Gems off of the planet. White stepped in while controlling her giant ship, mind controlled Yellow and Blue in a very disturbing sequence, and then the Crystal Gems engaged in an epic battle against the Diamond mech. They made it into her chamber, where she mind controls Garnet, Amethyst, and Pearl.

White tried to convince Steven he is Pink Diamond, but he wouldn't be manipulated into believing something that wasn't true. So, in a truly shocking moment, she removed his Gem, and he began to die. His Gem formed a powerful pink version of himself and told White, in no uncertain terms, that Pink was gone. Then, in a scene beautifully animated by legendary Disney animator James Baxter, Steven re-fused with his Gem. White begins throwing a tantrum that Steven calls out, which caused her to become embarrassed and realize the error of her ways and relinquish control of the others. They traveled back to Earth where the Diamonds cured the corrupted Gems. The episode, and the series, ended with Steven singing "Change Your Mind," a short but poignant song about loving yourself and not worrying about what others think. The episode was a fantastic and satisfying way to wrap up the series. It had everything that made Steven Universe so great, from its action to the superb vocal performances, but especially the emotional depth to the story and characters that so heavily defined the show from episode one.

What is your favorite episode of Steven Universe ? Discuss it down in the comments.
